figures.caption: Figure 2: (a) Shared LLaMA2-7B–SCRIBE variance is greater for concrete than abstract properties in all regions except LTC, whereas SCRIBE-unique variance does not differ systematically between the two groups. (b) Percentage decrease in shared (mean) and SCRIBE-unique variance (median) after removing the top 5, 10, or 20 properties ranked by their whole-brain leave-one-property-out effect on shared (left three columns) or SCRIBE-unique variance (right three columns). Asterisks indicate significant paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across participants.
Figure 3: Pearson correlations between SCRIBE properties at the TR level, ordered by hierarchical clustering (average linkage on 1− r).
Figure 4: Correlations between SCRIBE properties across content words (left), across TRs (middle, as in Figure 3), and across TRs after regressing out word rate (right), all in the same order.

Figure 5: Top-20 properties by mean whole-brain decrease in shared (left) and SCRIBE-unique variance (right) when each property is removed individually. Error bars: SEM across participants; numbers: participants showing a decrease.
